candidates.name: Your property boundaries - overview
verified_facts: There is usually no record of the exact boundary between two properties in England and Wales.
A title plan normally gives an idea of boundary position rather than an exact line.
More precise recording can use a boundary agreement or a determined-boundary application.
semantic_limits: General public boundary guidance is not an exact parcel geometry for terrain sampling.

candidates.name: Apply to record the exact boundary
verified_facts: A determined-boundary application is available for registered property.
The application requires supporting evidence, a DB form and a plan prepared by a chartered land surveyor.
Successful applications update the title plan and register.
semantic_limits: The application route does not prove these three parcels already have determined boundaries.

candidates.name: Exact line of boundary: registration (DB)
verified_facts: Form DB is HM Land Registry's application form for recording an exact line of boundary.
The page routes applicants to practice guide 40 supplement 4 for the detailed boundary requirements.
semantic_limits: Form DB is a workflow artifact, not an exact boundary result or terrain source.

candidates.name: Make a boundary agreement with your neighbour
verified_facts: A boundary agreement can use a written description, an Ordnance Survey map or a drawn map.
The agreement can be submitted for recording in the register using AP1.
semantic_limits: A recorded boundary agreement is not silently promoted to a section-60 determined boundary.

candidates.name: Other plan-related services and guides (PG40s6)
verified_facts: PG40 supplement 6 describes other HM Land Registry plan-related services and mapping guidance.
semantic_limits: Plan-service routing does not establish legal-boundary coordinates or elevation.

candidates.name: National Geoid Model OSGM15
verified_facts: OSGM15 transforms ETRS89 ellipsoid height to orthometric height and provides ODN heights on mainland Britain.
It is a 1km grid and values between nodes use bilinear interpolation.
OS gives nominal mainland-UK geoid-model accuracy of about 8mm rms.
semantic_limits: OSGM15 uncertainty is transformation uncertainty, not EA LiDAR RMSE or a source-accuracy gain.

candidates.name: National Grid Transformation OSTN15
verified_facts: OSTN15 is the definitive transformation between ETRS89 and OSGB36 National Grid.
It operates on horizontal easting/northing coordinates.
semantic_limits: OSTN15 is horizontal transformation evidence and is not counted as vertical terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: Future of British mapping coordinate systems
verified_facts: OSGB36 and ODN remain the basis of OS mapping.
OS Net with OSTN15 and OSGM15 provides GNSS access to national horizontal and vertical datums.
semantic_limits: Datum-access architecture establishes reference lineage, not parcel-specific terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: OS NGD coordinate reference systems
verified_facts: BNG EPSG:27700 is horizontal and does not include a vertical height reference.
BNG plus ODN height is represented as compound CRS EPSG:7405.
semantic_limits: EPSG:27700 geometry alone cannot prove the vertical datum of an elevation value.

candidates.name: Datum, ellipsoid and projection information
verified_facts: OS lists EPSG:27700 for BNG, EPSG:5701 for ODN vertical datum and EPSG:7405 for BNG plus ODN height.
OS also lists identifiers for OSTN15 and OSGM15 transformations.
semantic_limits: Reference identifiers define coordinate semantics, not measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: OS MasterMap Building Height Attribute - product data
verified_facts: Building Height Attribute data is derived from DTM and DSM sources.
Heights are supplied to one decimal metre and use ODN on mainland Britain with OSGM15 in the datum chain.
semantic_limits: Derived building height is not a bare-earth parcel DTM and output precision is not ground-height accuracy.

candidates.name: WCS standard registry
verified_facts: OGC lists WCS 2.1 Core and WCS 2.0 service extensions separately.
The registry lists Range Subsetting, Scaling, CRS, Interpolation, Processing and Transaction extensions.
Interpolation Extension 1.1 is listed as OGC 24-018r1.
semantic_limits: The standards registry establishes version/status routing only; it does not prove EA endpoint configuration or value accuracy.

candidates.name: WCS Scaling Extension 1.0
verified_facts: The approved WCS Scaling Extension changes a coverage grid by scaling.
Scaling can create range values from original locations and neighborhoods, so resampling/interpolation can be involved.
semantic_limits: Scaled output is derived and cannot be called native-resolution evidence without explicit proof.

candidates.name: WCS Interpolation Extension 1.1
verified_facts: Interpolation Extension 1.1 defines client control of interpolation during GetCoverage processing.
It defines interpolation and interpolation-per-axis conformance classes.
Interpolation can matter during subsetting, scaling and CRS transformation.
semantic_limits: Interpolation must be explicit; interpolated output is not silently treated as a native observation.

candidates.name: WCS Processing Extension 2.0
verified_facts: The WCS Processing Extension embeds coverage processing based on WCPS into WCS.
It enables server-side processing beyond simple native coverage retrieval.
semantic_limits: Processed output is derived unless the processing operation is explicitly part of the canonical measurement contract.

candidates.name: Web Processing Service 2.0
verified_facts: WPS 2.0 executes computing processes and describes their purpose and functionality.
Processes can combine raster, vector or coverage inputs with algorithms and can execute synchronously or asynchronously.
semantic_limits: WPS results are algorithmic outputs, not native terrain observations by default.

candidates.name: WCS XML/SOAP Protocol Binding Extension
verified_facts: The standard defines SOAP/XML client-server communication for WCS 2.0.
Its conformance target is the protocol binding for carrying WCS requests and responses.
semantic_limits: Protocol binding affects transport and encoding, not terrain accuracy, interpolation policy or survey lineage.

candidates.name: Testbed-12 OWS SOAP User Guide
verified_facts: The OGC guide explains that WCS protocol binding is separated from functions such as range subsetting or CRS transformation.
semantic_limits: This is non-normative implementation guidance and is used only for transport-versus-function separation.

candidates.name: OGC API - Maps - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API Maps defines map retrieval and subsetting controls including subset and subset-crs behavior.
semantic_limits: Rendered map output and map subsetting are excluded from numeric parcel elevation sampling.

candidates.name: OGC API - DGGS - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API DGGS defines retrieval by discrete global grid zones and supports subsetting for additional dimensions.
semantic_limits: DGGS zone addressing is not substituted for the native EPSG:27700 parcel raster grid.

candidates.name: OGC compliant implementations registry
verified_facts: OGC maintains a registry of products certified against standards including WCS Core and WCS service extensions.
semantic_limits: A third-party certification does not prove the Environment Agency endpoint uses that implementation or configuration.

candidates.name: Testbed-14 Swath Coverage Engineering Report
verified_facts: The engineering report references WCS 2.1, WCS 2.0.1, protocol bindings and coverage encoding standards in swath-coverage work.
semantic_limits: The engineering report is non-normative architecture/version context and cannot establish EA raster values or accuracy.
